facts.text: Manistee sits on an isthmus between Manistee Lake and Lake Michigan, with the Manistee River bisecting the city as it flows west to the latter.
During the lumber boom of the 1880s, Manistee was the headquarters of Manistee and North‑Eastern railroad and had more millionaires per capita than anywhere else in the U.S.
The Ramsdell Theatre, built in 1938, is an Art Deco venue that once hosted the Manistee Civic Players and later drew filmmaker Michael Moore for a restoration push.
Manistee’s name comes from an Ojibwe word meaning “river with islands at its mouth,” reflecting the city’s location on the Manistee River’s delta.
Three major factories—Packaging Corporation of America, Morton Salt, and Martin Marietta—anchor Manistee’s industrial landscape on Lake Manistee.
The Manistee National Forest surrounds the city, offering thousands of acres of forest, lakes, and rivers that define the region’s natural beauty.
